suggestedGuidanceUpdates.suggestion: Add a note about MTP + graph mode incompatibility on gfx908: when testing MTP speculative decoding on MI100, the FULL_DECODE_ONLY graph mode is incompatible with MTP (causes RuntimeError during graph capture). The worker must fall back to --enforce-eager for MTP testing. Workers should document this as a discovered blocking issue AND note that the eager fallback results in significant throughput regression (-25%+ vs baseline eager, and much worse vs graph mode). Future workers should skip MTP testing on gfx908 hardware unless the upstream vLLM MTP+graph incompatibility is resolved.
suggestedGuidanceUpdates.evidence: enable-mtp-speculative-decoding: MTP graph mode attempt failed 3 times with RuntimeError: cancelled. Eager fallback showed -25.7% throughput vs baseline eager (15.90 vs 21.39 tok/s at c1). This matches the pattern seen for other MI100 architectural limitations (gfx908 cluster_dims, SKINNY_GEMM, etc.).

rejectedObservations.observation: launch-mtp.sh defaults to graph mode which always fails on MI100; should default to --enforce-eager
rejectedObservations.reason: Non-blocking. The script has a --enforce-eager flag that works correctly. Changing the default could hide the graph incompatibility finding. The mtp-results.md clearly documents the incompatibility for future users. Not worth modifying at this stage.

The contract comparison is ambiguous - MTP forces eager mode, so comparing to eager baseline is the correct comparison. At +9.3% TPOT vs eager baseline, it barely fails the <=100% threshold. The worker correctly self-reported this. User testing validator will make the formal pass/fail determination. Not a code quality issue.
